entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Tritantaechmes, King of the Sagartians, played a pivotal role in the politics of the 6th century BCE region.

As ruler of Arbela, Tritantaechmes established trade relationships with neighboring regions, including the Lydian Empire. He claimed to be a descendant of Cyaxares of Media and his diplomatic efforts had far-reaching consequences.

Tritantaechmes' reign was marked by conflicts with the Neo-Babylonian Empire, which ultimately led to his downfall in 520 BCE. Despite this, he left a lasting legacy in the region.

The construction of the Royal Road, a vast network of trade routes, was a testament to his diplomatic prowess.

Tritantaechmes' diplomatic efforts paved the way for future interactions between the Sagartians and the Persian Empire.

The region's cultural and economic development was significantly influenced by his reign.

Tritantaechmes' diplomatic legacy extended beyond the region, shaping the course of international relations in the ancient world.

In the words of Herodotus, 'Tritantaechmes was a man of great wisdom and cunning, who was able to bring peace and prosperity to the region through his diplomatic efforts.'
